claim: The Hall(DC)+inductive-coil(AC) hybrid sensing architecture has direct prior art spanning 1999-2025: power electronics (HOKA probe), space magnetometry, fusion (JET RHP line and 2025 Kalman-fusion papers), and accelerator magnets.
limitations: Fusion-specific instances are concentrated in 2022-2025 within two overlapping author clusters (CERN/Arpaia; JET/Prague/KAERI).

claim: Correcting coil/integrator additive drift b_C with a non-integrating absolute reference (Hall, NMR, or magnet current) is hardware-proven (CERN bench: 59.9-120 ppm/s reduced to 0.02-0.08 ppm/s) and is the published design basis of ITER's outer-vessel steady-state sensor (OVSS) subsystem - 60 bismuth-Hall units complementing the inductive set for long-pulse operation (final design published and units manufactured; ITER is not yet operating).
limitations: None of these estimate or correct Hall sensitivity S_H from passive sensing. Stage-70 correction: P003's abstract contains only bismuth-sensor high-field qualification (no OVSS-pairing description) - the pairing claim now rests on H067/H068; 'system level' is design intent, not operating experience (former wording 'deployed at system level' retracted).

claim: No verified peer-reviewed source jointly estimates {B, S_H, b_H, K_C, b_C} from a Hall+coil pair with a stated identifiability condition; the strongest identifiability proof found (rank condition for state+bias+unknown input) explicitly excludes an unknown sensor-gain term.
limitations: Absence claim is bounded by the 10A search scope (7 domains); H021's own validation is simulation-only.

claim: In absolute+rate two-sensor fusion, joint bias/state observability is excitation-conditional, not automatic (GPS/INS requires maneuvering; magnetometer bias determination degenerates in unfavorable geometry). Inference: Hall+coil mutual calibration will require persistent excitation or an injected known field; this condition is unproven for the Hall+coil pair specifically.
limitations: GPS/INS and spacecraft-magnetometer analogs assume known absolute-sensor gain; the Hall case cannot.

claim: JET RHP in-situ co-packaged copper-microsolenoid AC self-test/recalibration (known injected field, synchronous detection) preserved InSb Hall sensitivity to SD ~0.07% over 11.5 years / >19,000 pulses including a D-T campaign; the same embedded microsolenoids double as inductive pickup coils whose signals are recorded during pulses.
limitations: Co-located, common-package, common current-reference chain: what the record proves stable is the product S_H*G_cal (die x winding); a common-mode (shared radiation/thermal) drift of die and reference winding together is undetectable by construction (stage-20 CASE E confound). Stage-70 note: 'same-die' in earlier wording was imprecise - the winding is a separate copper element in the same package.

claim: Existing Hall+coil drift correction does NOT prove PASSIVE in-situ Hall radiation-sensitivity calibration: every fusion-context instance either corrects the coil/integrator chain using the Hall channel as reference with S_H assumed known/stable, or recalibrates the Hall channel ACTIVELY via a known-current microsolenoid (C05 line). No source demonstrates passive, measurement-based coil-derived identification of radiation-induced Hall gain or bias drift in any fusion or radiation environment; in fusion the passive coil-to-Hall direction exists only as published proposals (H003 section 5 dry-run/ramp recalibration; ITER OVSS calibration plan, H067).
limitations: H059 (non-fusion HTS magnet, driven known ramp, no radiation) is the only demonstrated passive instance; H011 demonstrates the ACTIVE (actuator-injection) variant under fission-reactor irradiation to >1e18 n/cm2. The active-vs-passive distinction is load-bearing for every novelty statement built on this claim (stage-70 correction).

claim: Spinning-current offset cancellation reduces but does not eliminate Hall offset; a residual offset floor survives, so b_H remains a free parameter even with current spinning active.
limitations: Residual-floor magnitude for the user's specific GaN devices is not in the ledger.

claim: Embedded known-field calibration references exist at chip scale (on-chip reference actuator next to a Hall array, ~392 mT/A per coil) and machine scale (HBT-EP 'artificial plasma' calibration coils used to calibrate 216 Mirnov coils and a Rogowski coil in situ).
limitations: H038's quantitative figures are search-snippet-sourced (flagged for full-text read); H040 calibrates inductive sensors, not a Hall channel.

claim: Validation-strength inversion: the fusion Kalman-fusion papers architecturally closest to the mission's proposal are synthetic-data-only or validation-unconfirmed, while the strongest hardware validations are non-fusion and do not address Hall gain.
limitations: H002's validation basis could not be confirmed (publisher blocked); it may contain more than the abstract shows.

claim: In superconducting-magnet quench detection, Hall-array and coil (quench-antenna) approaches remain parallel, unfused research lines even in well-resourced programs - a counter-signal against assuming Hall+coil fusion is trivial engineering.
limitations: Two sources, one sub-domain; absence of fusion there does not prove difficulty, only non-adoption.

claim: The reverse correction direction - coil channel calibrating the Hall channel in situ from PASSIVELY measured signals - is demonstrated (abstract-confirmed) in exactly one non-fusion case: the Feather-M2 HTS dipole's cryogenic Hall sensors were cross-calibrated in situ against induction-coil sensors during driven magnet ramps. In fusion the same direction is published as PROPOSAL only: H003 section 5 (passive recalibration via dry runs/plasma ramp-up) and the ITER OVSS calibration plan (H067: readjust OVSS sensitivity against outer-vessel inductive coils during current ramps).
limitations: H059: non-fusion, no radiation, engineered excitation, quantitative accuracy figures not read (abstract-level). The fusion instances are unrealized plans - no demonstration exists (C06). H067's cross-calibration sentence is search-index body text (abstract independently verified; full text not accessed) - flagged.

claim: InSb Hall sensitivity degrades under a thermal-inclusive fission neutron spectrum but remains stable under a purely fast-neutron spectrum at comparable fluence (R001: ~1e16 n/cm2 in both facilities); follow-up thermal-type-reactor irradiation series at 8.7e17 and 1.2e18 n/cm2 support the same mechanism (R002); the authors attribute the difference to transmutation (In/Sb thermal-neutron capture) rather than displacement damage.
limitations: Both papers come from the same collaboration (limited independence); numeric degradation magnitudes were not accessible. Stage-70 precision fix: R001's ~1e16 two-spectrum comparison and R002's ~1e18 thermal-series are different fluence regimes - do not quote as one number.

claim: Quantified fast-neutron damage at ~6.6-7.0e17 n/cm2 (sample ~200 C): InSb thin-film Hall mobility fell 75-90% (average 83%, 9 samples), carrier-density change direction doping-dependent; graphene-on-SiC mobility fell 43% and sheet density 39% under the same exposure.
limitations: Single campaign/facility (MARIA reactor); bias state during exposure not specified.

claim: No bare GaN/AlGaN Hall-plate device has been irradiated and reported in the peer-reviewed literature under any neutron spectrum (fission, fast, or 14 MeV D-T); all GaN neutron evidence is HEMT/2DEG-structure or AlN-ceramic enabling physics.
limitations: This is the largest direct-evidence gap for the user's own device family; absence bounded by the 10B search scope (8 domains).

claim: AlGaN/GaN 2DEG proton damage is quantified (2 MeV, 6e14 cm-2: mobility -28.9%, 2DEG density -12.1%, interface broadened 2.2 nm); AlGaN/GaN micro-Hall sensors are only slightly affected at ~1e13 p/cm2 with degradation rising at higher fluence and PARTIAL recovery on annealing.
limitations: R012/R013/R015 quantitative conditions are secondary-sourced (publisher blocked); R022 figures are Crossref-abstract-confirmed.

claim: NIEL-based proton-to-gamma damage scaling under-predicts Co-60 gamma lifetime damage by ~14x in InAs/InAsSb, because proton cascade defects self-anneal more efficiently than gamma-produced isolated Frenkel pairs. Cross-species extrapolation is unsafe for III-V Hall materials.
limitations: One material family (InAs/InAsSb infrared detectors), minority-carrier-lifetime metric - mechanism argument transfers to Hall parameters only as a labeled inference.

claim: Mixed neutron+gamma damage is non-additive, and the direction of the non-additivity depends on device structure and the electrical quantity examined (GaN HEMT leakage sub-additive vs cascode threshold super-additive; bipolar op-amp offset synergistic).
limitations: Two device classes only; no Hall-device combined-field dataset exists (see C14/C21).

claim: A metallic (copper-active-layer) Hall sensor on ceramic substrate showed no measurable sensitivity change up to ~1e18 n/cm2 fission-spectrum fluence, with sensitivity flat over 100-250 C. Inference: metallic Hall is a candidate material-diverse reference channel for a semiconductor Hall+coil system.
limitations: Single source, abstract-level access, single fluence/temperature envelope; the inference (use as reference channel) is this mission's, not the paper's.

claim: Radiation-induced EMF (RIEMF) in mineral-insulated cables is an established additive error mechanism for coil signal chains (five-paper cluster, 1997-2004; ITER aims to keep non-inductive voltage well below 1 uV for 3000-s pulses per secondary-sourced figures).
limitations: No dose-to-RIEMF-magnitude curve could be independently confirmed (publisher access blocked); the 1 uV figure is secondary-sourced.

claim: The JET fibre-optic current sensor (FOCS) operated through the DTE2 D-T campaign (~8.5e20 total neutrons): Verdet constant +/-4% shot-to-shot, a possible ~0.7% campaign-scale drift at low statistical confidence, no disqualifying degradation, continuously cross-validated against the Continuous External Rogowski - the only in-machine D-T radiation-effects dataset in the ledger, and a template for what Hall+coil qualification would need to produce.
limitations: FOCS is a Faraday-effect optical sensor, not a Hall device; transfer of its qualification template to Hall+coil is a proposal, not evidence.

claim: In-situ (during-irradiation) recalibration of Hall sensitivity against a material-diverse PASSIVE field-sensor reference is unreported for any Hall material, in any source found by either the radiation or hybrid lane. Actuator-based in-situ recalibration against a co-packaged copper-winding known-field reference IS reported: during fission-reactor irradiation to >1e18 n/cm2 and through JET operation (H011; C05 line).
limitations: Bounded by 10A+10B search scope. Stage-70 correction: the surviving gap is specifically the passive witness-SENSOR architecture (stage-30 Option D), not 'in-situ recalibration' per se - novelty statements must make this distinction explicitly.

claim: GaN-family TID response has two regimes: a rapidly-annealing low-dose threshold shift (<3 krad(SiO2)) common to HEMT and MOS-HEMT, and a persistent oxide-trapping shift extending to at least 2 Mrad in MOS-HEMTs only; a 200 C / 25 min anneal partially recovers gamma-degraded transport.
limitations: R024 uses 10 keV X-rays as TID surrogate (not gamma); R033 is peer_review_uncertain (ECS Transactions proceedings).

claim: Heavily irradiated III-V material converges toward a material-specific limiting Fermi level (InAs to n+-type, InSb to p-type, under 5-10 MeV protons at 2e16 cm-2), consistent with Fermi-level-stabilization theory. Inference: radiation-induced InSb/InAs Hall parameter drift may asymptote (bounded) rather than diverge - a falsifiable model input, unconfirmed under neutron exposure.
limitations: Proton-only evidence; R042 warns cross-species scaling within III-Vs can err by an order of magnitude, so the neutron-case asymptote must be tested, not assumed.

claim: Transmutation is a permanent (non-annealable at service temperatures) damage channel: thermal-neutron Ga-to-Ge conversion in GaN required a 950 C activation anneal; In/Sb thermal-neutron capture is the attributed driver of InSb fission-spectrum sensitivity loss.
limitations: R025 is a doping demonstration on bulk GaN, not a sensor-degradation study; the permanence-in-service conclusion is a labeled inference from the 950 C figure.

claim: Readout-chain radiation failure modes are distinct from sensor-die damage and must be budgeted separately: bipolar op-amp offset/bias-current degradation with neutron+gamma synergy; millisecond-scale single-event transients originating in op-amp bias/startup circuitry; COTS ADC TID/SEU evaluation exists as methodology; the only 1-MGy-class rad-hard instrumentation-amplifier design found is simulation-only.
limitations: Most quantitative thresholds are secondary-sourced or unread (publisher access); R050 must never be cited as experimental validation.

claim: Activation-foil dosimetry is a mature, validated fluence-monitoring practice: VERDI detectors benchmarked at a 14 MeV D-T reference field (C/E = 1.05 +/- 0.13) and then validated in-machine at JET D-D to 8% agreement; the two-step protocol (reference-field calibration, then in-machine validation) is the model for any Hall irradiation campaign's dosimetry.
limitations: Foil dosimetry gives fluence/spectrum, not sensor-parameter drift; surrogate-facility flux can sit 3-5 orders of magnitude below the target environment (R074).

claim: ITER's OVSS is the strongest real-machine-DESIGN precedent for pairing a DC Hall subsystem with the inductive set: 60 bismuth-Hall pair units on the vacuum vessel outer shell (final design published, units manufactured; ITER not yet operating). The published OVSS calibration plan additionally foresees the REVERSE direction - readjusting slowly-reducing OVSS sensitivity by cross-calibration against outer-vessel inductive coils during plasma current ramps (H067). It is a system-level pairing of separate sensor heads, not a co-located single-package hybrid; neither direction of the pairing has operated on any tokamak yet.
limitations: Stage-70 correction: former single-source anchoring on P003 removed (its abstract is sensor qualification only); H067's cross-calibration sentence is body-level search-index text, flagged; 'precedent' is design-stage - there is no operating-tokamak experience for either direction.

claim: Persistent-mode superconducting/HTS magnets are a documented poor fit: a coil is structurally blind to a static trapped field (no dB/dt after magnetization), and the field's accepted precision reference for that state is NMR, not a coil (persistent-mode NMR magnet held >2 years at ~3e-5 ppm/h drift with NMR cross-check).
limitations: Counterevidence limited to the brief magnetization transient itself, where pickup coils and Hall arrays are both used (P039, P049).

claim: Accelerator-magnet metrology already combines Hall probes + rotating/fixed coils + NMR as decades-old production practice, including in-situ calibration of rotating coils against a reference magnet - direct prior art that vetoes any architecture-level novelty claim in that domain.
limitations: Bench/test-stand context without fusion-grade radiation; the radiation/in-situ-embedded angle remains open (C36).

claim: Z-pinch/pulsed-power practice solved its redundancy need by cross-calibrating and fusing two inductive sensors (B-dot + Rogowski, +/-13-15%), deliberately bypassing Hall sensors; Hall-effect current sensors are independently documented as EMI-susceptible (tangential RF E-field) in power-electronics testing.
limitations: The EMI-susceptibility-to-z-pinch transfer is an explicit inference (power-electronics test conditions, not a z-pinch measurement); ns-us timescales leave no DC baseline for a Hall channel to anchor.

claim: Magnetoresistive alternatives compete directly on the DC+broadband axis: TMR sensors span DC-to-broadband in one channel and showed no key-parameter degradation to 5 Mrad(Si) gamma/X-ray under bias; AMR tolerated 200 krad(Si) gamma with the front-end electronics as the weaker element.
limitations: Gamma/X-ray only - no neutron displacement-damage evidence for TMR/AMR was found; P063 was upgraded to verified at 10D after its author list was resolved.

claim: Stellarator field verification relies on electron-beam flux-surface mapping during commissioning (vacuum only, cannot coexist with plasma) plus trim-coil correction informed by it; no literature exists on a Hall+coil hybrid for stellarator field mapping.
limitations: The absence cuts both ways: an open niche for the user's HSX context, but zero prior validation to build on. Stage-70 addition: adjacent TOKAMAK commissioning practice exists and must be cited-and-distinguished - KSTAR measured field errors with an e-beam plus Hall sensor arrays in addition to pickup coils (P077, snippet-level content); e-beam mapping remains the entrenched, higher-accuracy stellarator incumbent.

claim: Long-pulse/steady-state magnetic diagnostics need non-inductive DC sensing as a design requirement, not a preference: DEMO's antimony-Hall steady-state program states inductive sensors 'require supplementation'; DEMO-class printed coils are qualified to >=500 C; WEST rebuilt its 469-sensor suite for ~1000-s pulses.
limitations: JT-60SA's 200 C / 9 MGy in-vessel figures (P006) are secondary-sourced and unconfirmed at full text.

claim: Fibre-optic (Faraday) current sensing is a credible competing upgrade path for tokamak current measurement (ITER FOCS accuracy limited by Faraday-mirror imperfections with a published compensation route; T-15MD concept; JET DTE2 validation) - EMI-immune, integrator-free, DC-capable.
limitations: FOCS measures enclosed current, not local field - it competes with Rogowski/current diagnostics, not with local field mapping.

claim: Where the environment already forced practitioners to abandon magnetic probes entirely (MagLIF load region uses optical PDV for peak current; hot dense pinch column uses spectroscopic Zeeman splitting), a Hall+coil hybrid adds no survivability and is out of scope.
limitations: Two sub-domains; the boundary is physical survivability, not sensing principle.

claim: Novelty constraints after direct prior-art analysis: architecture-level 'Hall+coil hybrid' is NOT novel (C01, C29). The credible remaining gaps, each narrowed at stage 70: (a) a joint gain+bias+state identifiability proof for the Hall+coil pair - no such analysis found through 2026 (H021 excludes sensor gain; aerospace magnetometer scale-factor/bias observability work relies on a known-field/attitude mechanism and must be scoped against); (b) hardware-validated PASSIVE bidirectional mutual correction in a real plasma and/or radiation environment - the CONCEPT is published prior art (H003 section 5; ITER OVSS calibration plan H067) and ACTIVE microsolenoid recalibration under D-T/fission irradiation is demonstrated (C05, H011), so what remains open is the passive demonstration plus its identifiability treatment; (c) in-situ radiation-aware Hall recalibration against a material-diverse PASSIVE witness sensor (actuator-winding recalibration is demonstrated, H011); (d) the stellarator-mapping application niche (no stellarator instance found; adjacent KSTAR Hall-array+coil commissioning practice P077 must be distinguished).
limitations: Each gap is an absence claim bounded by this mission's search scope; a dedicated prior-art search should precede any publication claim on gaps (a)-(d). Stage-70 addition: 2009/2010 patents on combined sensors for in-situ Hall calibration (GB2427700/FR2887991 formats, via H003 refs 66-67, discovery-level) mean a PATENT search is mandatory before any embedded-actuation novelty claim.

claim: Sequencing: validating the Hall channel first, then hybridizing, remains a defensible engineering order (a working calibrated Hall channel is a prerequisite for any fused system), but hybridization itself must not be the headline novelty claim; the contribution should target the C36 gaps.
limitations: Scope decision belongs to the user/advisor; this stage records the evidence-side constraints only.
